card: This pull request raises the minimum C++ standard for Bitcoin Core from C++20 to C++23, setting minimum compiler requirements to GCC 13 and Clang 19 across CMake, depends, and CI. It retires custom polyfills like util::Expected and custom byteswap implementations in favor of std::expected and std::byteswap, while also applying modern idioms like std::string::contains widely across the codebase. The author argues that keeping C++20 forces the accumulation of workarounds even as ecosystem dependencies like libmultiprocess adopt C++23. This RFC draft unblocks work tracked in #34979.
changed_since_previous: Added minor test adjustments for `std::expected` compliance and an IWYU fix, with no major changes to the overall approach.
evidence: PR description: 'C++23 for Bitcoin Core is mostly a "style update" on top of C++20. However, the workarounds to avoid C++23 keep accumulating and some parts of the code already use C++23 features, such as lambda attributes'
PR description notes minimum compiler bumps: 'GCC: 13, Clang: 19' and points to unlocked features discussed in #34979
problem: Maintaining C++20 compatibility forces developers to keep custom polyfills and workaround templates in-tree, while dependent projects like libmultiprocess already rely on C++23 features.

risk.why: Bumping compiler toolchain requirements and swapping fundamental utility types like byteswap and expected could cause subtle platform-specific build failures or runtime regressions across release binaries.

scope_notes: This RFC draft contains mechanical clang-tidy modernizations (`readability-container-contains`) across over 50 files alongside the build system bumps and standard library replacements.
summary: This PR raises the minimum C++ standard from C++20 to C++23 across CMake, depends, and CI, bumping the minimum required compiler versions to GCC 13 and Clang 19. It removes in-tree polyfills and workarounds by migrating `util::Expected` to `std::expected`, adopting `std::byteswap`, removing the `ALWAYS_FALSE` template workaround, and applying C++23 idioms such as `std::string::contains` and `std::views::zip` across the codebase.
